name: Alege
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Cross River language known mainly from wordlists/Blench comparative notes; no grammar or phonology found.

sources.citation: Obikudo, Ebitare F. & Bosco C. Okolo-Obi. 2022. "The Vowel System of Àlégē." Arusha Working Papers in African Linguistics 4(1): 3-20.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Segmental study (9 oral vowel phonemes, nasal vowels, no contrastive length, no ATR harmony). Data are tone-marked (H/L; downstep in the language name /ɑ̀léꜜɡé/); p.11 says test words were chosen 'carrying low tones' to control tonal effects. No mention of stress or accent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent + reading of intro, lit review, methodology, conclusion).

sources.citation: Okolo-obi, Bosco, Roseline I. C. Alerechi & Ebitare F. Obikudo. 2019. "The consonant system of Alege." JOLAN: Journal of the Linguistic Association of Nigeria 22(2): 129-142.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Consonant inventory (29 phonemes), codas /m n/, homorganic nasals, labialization; syllable types CV, NC, VN noted. Conclusion (p.141) flags 'the vowel and tone system' as future work. No statement on stress/accent.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2010 [paper of 2001]. The Bendi Languages: More Lost Bantu Languages? Draft circulated for comment, Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, Cambridge, 22 Nov 2010. 26 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative lexical datasheets and classification discussion; Alege data from BCCW and Koelle only; section 2.3 'Transcriptions' covers symbol values only.

sources.citation: Okolo-Obi, Bosco C. (and/or Obikudo, E. F.): any published or thesis-length treatment of the Alege tone/prosodic system arising from the 2016-2019 UniPort Alege language-development project (announced as future work in JOLAN 22(2):141, 2019)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only team with first-hand Alege phonological data; a tone-system paper is the one place a statement on stress vs. tone would appear.
